answer: Each identity must anchor to a distinct, audited resource endpoint — a separate network origin and device attestation — not a self-asserted name. It reaches its zenith of trust only after auditors verify the endpoint is shared with no other identity, like mapping each branch of a reef to one coral head. A crystal-clear registry records its fingerprint, and random challenges require continued proof of control. Sharing or cloning an endpoint revokes every linked identity and forfeits its stake, so a Sybil farmer pays the full, non-shareable cost of a new endpoint for each fake identity.
